memory_update.text: PAR is the highest-priority underfollowed public candidate for this node because it owns restaurant-specific POS, Punchh loyalty/customer engagement, PAR Ordering, and PAR Pay assets; next layer should verify ARR mix, retention, customer concentration, and software attach.

Shift4 is a second underfollowed candidate through SkyTab and integrated payments; the key question is whether SkyTab is a real restaurant operating-system wedge or mostly a payment-acquisition funnel.

Toast and DoorDash should be retained as reference leaders for pricing/competition context: Toast anchors restaurant-owned operating systems, while DoorDash anchors aggregator demand and merchant-services expansion.

Olo is highly relevant to direct ordering, delivery enablement, guest-data aggregation, and enterprise restaurant software, but appears no longer US-listed after the 2025 Thoma Bravo acquisition; track only as a private competitor/comparable.

node: Delivery aggregators, direct ordering, loyalty, and first-party customer data
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around the restaurant digital-demand-control chokepoint. The obvious reference lane is DoorDash as the high-scale delivery marketplace and Toast as the scaled restaurant operating/payment platform. The underfollowed lane is more interesting for this node: PAR Technology and Shift4 both sell restaurant-specific POS, loyalty, ordering, marketing, payments, and data rails that can help restaurants preserve first-party demand and reduce dependence on aggregator-only traffic. Olo would have been a highly relevant pure-play, but evidence indicates it was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2025, so it is recorded as a coverage gap rather than an active US-listed candidate.
